title: Copilots compete for software budgets while autopilots sell completed work
text: Software tools address a global software market of roughly $500 billion, whereas businesses spend over $10 trillion annually on services and labor. Buying copilot licenses treats AI as a tooling line-item that assists existing workers, whereas autopilots sell completed end-work directly. Confusing a tooling purchase with workflow delegation obscures the actual economic shift from software seat-licensing to labor substitution.
qualification: Venture capital market sizing and positioning thesis; draws a stylized contrast between tool procurement and services budgets that requires operational scrutiny in enterprise workflows.

public_locator.value: A copilot sells the tool. An autopilot sells the work... Software is a ~$500B market, services is a ~$10T market.
